title: Contrast Runner: staged A/B harness for model version comparison with automatic diagnostics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Build a modular A/B harness (Contrast Runner) that enables safe, measurable comparison of model versions with fine-grained exposure control and automated rollback triggers. The runner must support: (1) deterministic cohort assignment, (2) traffic-slice scheduling (time-of-day, geo, user segment), (3) multi-metric statistical checks (latency, toxicity, answer divergence, custom business metrics), and (4) automated restore policies when tests fail thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- API to declare experiment: variant definitions (model refs), traffic policy, metrics to monitor, statistical test configs, and fallback policy.
- Live traffic splitter capable of shadowing and mirrored evaluations without affecting response path for control.
- Statistical engine that runs sequential hypothesis tests with configurable alpha spending and supports A/B and multi-arm comparisons.
- Auto-rollback action that triggers a circuit-breaker and reassigns traffic to baseline, with audit log, alerting, and ticket stub.
- Dashboard surfaces per-variant risk scores, per-metric p-values, sample sizes, and drift indicators.
- End-to-end integration tests + canary run on staging with synthetic workload.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
We prefer sequential testing with alpha spending (e.g., O'Brien-Fleming) to avoid repeated-hypothesis inflation; allow conservative default thresholds and permit PM override per-experiment. To minimize cost, initial phases should use lightweight shadowing (no forwarding) for classification-style models and gradually ramp to live traffic. For high-latency models, introduce latency budgeting and cap sample sizes so experiments do not degrade SLAs.

Observability & telemetry:
- Emit per-variant events (assign, serve, compare, fallback) and sample-level signals for post-hoc analysis.
- Integrate with Console dashboards: experiment timeline, metric heatmaps, per-route token-cost delta.

Security & compliance:
- Experiments that touch PII must default to shadow-only mode and require security_review_required=true.

Dependencies:
- runtime routing primitives (ENG-2041), console visualization components (ENG-3187), metric ingestion and eval pipeline (PM-30456).

updates: 2025-11-05: Initial scoping completed; decided on sequential testing model; put alpha spending math into design doc.
2025-12-10: Spike concluded — traffic-slicer MVP routes by hashed user_id and geo; discovered race with KV cache in serving runtime; raised ENG-4192.
2026-01-22: UX workshop with Console team — prioritized experiment timeline view and per-variant cost delta. Design feedback: add quick-rollback button and audit trail.
2026-02-18: Security reviewed shadow-only default for experiments that include PII—security_review_required flag added to API contract.
2026-02-28: Prototype PR opened for traffic-splitter and cohort assignment; integration tests failing intermittently on store TTLs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/contrast-runner/pull/12

2026-03-10: PM/Eng sync — agreed on canary ramp plan for staging: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% with checkpoints at each step. Added metric guard: if latency p95 increases > 15% or divergence score > 0.25, trigger rollback.
notes: Work should be extensible to support multi-arm comparisons and future cohorts. Keep experiment artifacts exportable for offline statistical audits. Consider exposing a safe sandbox mode for partners to run private experiments.
